CSE-4012                                                                                                                 about:srcdoc  
  
  
  Exam Date & Time: 08-May-2024 (02:30 PM - 05:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MIT BLR - BTech VI Semester - End Semester Examination - April / May -2024  
  Bio-Informatics [CSE-4012]  
  Marks: 50                                                                               Duration: 180 mins.  
  PART-A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1)           Discuss in detail at least five characteristics of a Good Biological Database. List and  
  interpret at least three features of the GenBank Nucleotide Database.  
  (4)  
  A)  
  B)      Enumerate and elaborate on the six steps that are adapted by the UniProtKB Database  
  for automatic annotation. Bring out the significance and need of Biological databases      (4)  
  which are highly specific to a specialized micro-domain.  
  
  C)      Determine the highest matched score for aligning GGTAA and ATGTC using a simple  
  matrix-driven alignment strategy.                                                          (2)  
  
  2)           Distinguish between Global Alignment and Local Alignment. Illustrate the steps in the  
  Smith-Waterman algorithm to justify Local Alignment between a pair of nucleotide  
  (4)  
  bases.  
  A)  
  B)      Illustrate the working of DbClustal for progressive alignment and iterative alignment  
  which involves two sets of iterations in the context of gene sequence alignment.           (4)  
  
  C)      In the context of bioinformatics analyses, interpret the need for Format Conversion by  
  citing a tool as an example.                                                               (2)  
  
  3)           State and interpret at least one exhaustive and one heuristic strategy for multiple  
  sequence alignment of biological sequences.  
  (4)  
  A)  
  B)      Discuss the concepts of Maximum Parsimony and Bootstrapping along with the  
  schematic representation of a bootstrap analysis for the construction and evaluation of    (4)  
  phylogenetic trees.  
  
  C)      State and interpret the Shimodaira-Hasegawa test along with an equation in the context  
  of guide trees.                                                                            (2)

  4)              With an illustration using a flow diagram, discuss the overview of the MUSTANG  
  algorithm. Also, give the configuration setup for the implementation of the MUSTANG  
  (5)  
  algorithm by specifying the dependent factors.  
  A)  
  B)         With the help of necessary diagrammatic depictions, discuss the role of Bioinformatics  
  in drug discovery focusing on its applications in drug metabolism, pharmacology, and      (5)  
  toxicology.  
  
  5)              With an abstract architecture of Bio2RDF knowledge system framework, illustrate and  
  elaborate on the integration of bioinformatics tools with associated knowledge via  
  Ontological Design, Structured NameSpaces, and Triple Stores. Also, explain the need      (5)  
  A)         of Rdfizer programs for Semantic Integration of Bio information and Derived  
  Knowledge.  
  
  B)         With an illustration of the steps involved in RaptorX, discuss the protein structure  
  prediction using the Threading Method. Also, elaborate on the results and interpretation  
  for prediction of secondary and tertiary protein structures. List the steps adapted by   (5)  
  Open PSIPRED for secondary protein structure prediction.  
  
  
  -----End-----
